evidence_levels.documented: stated in a cited source (Verne's reported words, firsthand observation, or reliable reference)
evidence_levels.inferred: reasoned from multiple sources; see reasoning
evidence_levels.speculative: plausible but weakly or not supported by collected sources

citations.quote: was born in Nantes on the 8th of February, 1828
born at Nantes on the 8th of February 1828
est né à Nantes le 8 février 1828

records.claim: His father (Pierre Verne) was a lawyer, educated in Paris, who wrote songs privately and avoided publicity; his mother was Breton, from Morlaix (per Verne).
records.caveats: Sherard's interview is Verne's speech as reported/translated by a journalist; some dates in it are wrong (e.g. Five Weeks is dated 1861 and Verne's age at writing as 25; actual publication Jan 1863, Verne aged 34).

citations.quote: My mother was a Bas;Bretonne, from Morlaix
He wrote songs at a time when songs were still written in France

records.claim: He was one of five children (two boys, three girls); his brother Paul (naval officer, later Alpine writer) was his closest friend.

citations.quote: My brother Paul was and is my dearest friend
His brother, Paul Verne, contributed to the Transactions of the French Alpine Club

records.claim: Educated at the lycée of Nantes, then sent to Paris to study law.

citations.quote: was educated at the Lycée of Nantes, where I remained till I had finished my rhetoric classes, when I was sent to Paris to study law
he went to Paris to study for the bar

records.claim: His early literary career was in the theatre; Les Pailles rompues (with Dumas fils' involvement) was staged at the Gymnase (1850). He was secretary of the Théâtre Lyrique.

citations.quote: in 1850 his verse comedy, Les Pailles rompues, in which Alexandre Dumas fils had some share, was produced at the Gymnase
I was then secretary to the Lyric Theatre

records.claim: He speculated on the Paris Bourse in the 1850s; by his own account it taught him 'the romance of commerce' used in his novels.
records.caveats: Sherard's interview is Verne's speech as reported/translated by a journalist; some dates in it are wrong (e.g. Five Weeks is dated 1861 and Verne's age at writing as 25; actual publication Jan 1863, Verne aged 34).

citations.quote: it was there that I got to know the romance of commerce, the fever of business

records.claim: First published novel, Cinq semaines en ballon, published by Hetzel (Jan 1863), beginning a lifelong publishing relationship with P.-J. Hetzel and later his son.
records.caveats: Sherard's text dates it 1861; Claretie gives 1863 (correct).

citations.quote: Ce fut en 1863 que Jules Verne publia, chez Hetzel, son premier « roman scientifique »
I sent the manuscript to the well-known Paris publisher, M. Hetzel

records.claim: Married Honorine (née Morel), widow de Viane with two daughters, whom he met at Amiens; they had one son, Michel.
records.caveats: Marriage date (10 Jan 1857, Paris) and her maiden name come from modern biographies not in the corpus; Sherard's OCR spells 'de Vianne'.

citations.quote: was a widow with two little daughters
Our only child, Michel, lives in Paris

records.claim: Owned successive yachts named Saint-Michel (a small fishing-type sailboat, later a ~100-ton steam yacht) and cruised the Channel, North Sea and Mediterranean.

citations.quote: le Saint-Michel, est devenu un yacht à vapeur d’une centaine de tonneaux
comes from a tour from Tangiers to Malta on my yacht

records.claim: Travelled to America in 1867 aboard the Great Eastern, visiting New York, Albany and Niagara (his only US visit).

citations.quote: came from my voyage to America in 1867, on the Great Eastern
For a few days only, during which time I saw Niagara

records.claim: In 1886 his mentally ill nephew shot him in the leg, leaving him permanently lame and ending his long travels.
records.caveats: Nephew's name (Gaston Verne) and date (9 March 1886) come from modern biography, not corpus.

citations.quote: drew a revolver and fired at me, wounding me in the left leg and laming me for life
walks with a slight limp, the result of a wound

records.claim: Settled permanently in Amiens, lived at the corner of Boulevard Longueville and Rue Charles-Dubois, and served on the Amiens municipal council.

citations.quote: Jules Verne lives on the Boulevard Longueville, at Amiens, at the corner of the Rue Charles Dubois
I am far prouder of being a town councillor of Amiens than of my literary reputation

records.claim: Made Officer of the Légion d'honneur (1892); never elected to the Académie française although some of his books were crowned by it.

citations.quote: My promotion to officer was signed in July of last year
he was never enrolled among its members
He died at Amiens on the 24th of March 1905

records.claim: Suffered in old age from weakening eyesight and gastric pain ('gastralgia').

citations.quote: there are days when gastralgia martyrizes him
